extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard leadership, MLCPAC contract specialists, Contracting Officer's Technical Representatives (COTRs), and other Coast Guard contract administrators involved in A-76 service contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and findings for evaluating A-76 (OMB Circular A-76) service contracts in the U.S. Coast Guard, focusing on cost comparisons with the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO), contract administration, specifications, post-award monitoring, and perceptions of unit leadership. Useful for auditors, contract specialists, and unit commanders assessing A-76 outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of contract file documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: These contract files should have been able to stand on their own for later review; files must fully explain why some actions were taken and others were not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract files transferred to MLCPAC lacked sufficient explanation for actions; post-award record keeping must be standardized so Contract Specialists can verify actions and decisions later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award contract maintenance procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no standard Coast Guard contract post-award maintenance procedure, which has resulted in contract inconsistencies and added work for the Contract Specialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and implement a standard post-award maintenance system to avoid transfer discrepancies, ensure consistent record keeping, and reduce added administrative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and verification of deductions for unsatisfactory performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Deductions for unsatisfactory contract performance must be recorded as a reduction in cost in the contract record and be verifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some MLCPAC contracts had deductions not recorded in a verifiable manner; require consistent accounting entries and retain supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR training sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The training received by the Contracting Officer's Technical Representative (COTR) may be insufficient for their assigned duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses provided good basic contracting knowledge but little training on day-to-day COTR duties, lessons learned, and specific quality assurance methods; training should cover practical COTR functions and QA techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of specifications and Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications and contractor performance should be adequate for the contracted-out activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units often lack expertise to write adequate service contract specifications; inexperienced personnel at unit level can produce inadequate PWSs—use experienced writers and review for flexibility to anticipate changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance and contract monitoring competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons assigned to monitor contracts must be adequately trained in quality assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments indicated lack of properly trained QA personnel; ensure contract monitors/COTRs receive QA training and oversight to evaluate contractor performance reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command control over contracted activity (timeliness of responses/remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The command must have adequate control over the contracted-out activity: responses and remedies to problems should be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems identified include administrative delays, distance to contract administration, and slow MLCPAC responses; consider local contracting officer administration to improve timeliness and control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of contractor performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor performance should meet contract specifications and provide acceptable service quality (e.g., food quality, security performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance depends on contractor management and local project managers; some facilities had improved food quality while certain security performance was marginal—monitor performance consistently and consider manager qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship quality between command and contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: The command's overall relationship with the civilian contractor should be professional and congenial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All interviewed commands believed relationships were generally congenial and professional; professionalism, responsiveness, and good project management are indicators of a positive relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate performer selection (military/civilian employee vs contractor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the commercial activity is best conducted by military, Government civilian employees, or a civilian contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include flexibility, instant response, multi-mission capability, continuity, availability of qualified personnel, administrative burden, and cost. Many COs/XOs preferred Government employees for security and some preferred contractors for continuity/cost in housing maintenance and some food services.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO staffing adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) must be staffed adequately to correctly perform the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All MEO winners interviewed reported needing more personnel; causes include lean workforce, non-rate shortages, or MEOs purposely undercut—reevaluate MEO staffing and recompetition if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and availability of current MEO cost data after award
rubrics_metrics.description: Current MEO costs should be available to MLCPAC Contract Specialists after the contract is awarded to determine if Government cost savings continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEO costs were not available post-award, preventing accurate determination of continued savings; ensure MEO cost reporting/availability post-award and update comparisons when scopes change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring of funding levels against actual contract costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding levels allocated based on original contract value must be monitored and changed as contract costs increase or decrease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCG Headquarters allocates funds based on original contract value but does not adjust as actual costs change, creating budget risks; implement ongoing monitoring and reallocation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation and verification of Government cost savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Government cost savings for A-76 contracts must be accurate and account for changes in contract cost over the performance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present savings are computed using initial award price and pre-A-76 Government cost; they are not revised for actual contract cost changes—recompute savings periodically to reflect real performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract award decision threshold per OMB Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: To award a contract to the private sector, the contractor's price must be lower than the Government MEO's personnel-related cost by 10%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Base Ketchikan original contract price was only 5.4% less than MEO and therefore should not have been awarded; enforce the 10% threshold in award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for returning activity in-house under A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-76 contract to return in-house, Government cost must be below the contractor's cost by 10% (for a combined 20% below MEO) plus 25% of the contractor's capital assets cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stated percentages when evaluating whether to bring an activity back in-house; ensure calculations include capital asset adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and challenge of Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: DOL wage determinations used in bids should be questioned and validated when questionable since inaccurate determinations can distort contract cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Center Alameda security contract had a possibly low/inaccurate DOL determination that made contractor costs appear favorable; MLCPAC should review unusual wage determinations before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-change review and MEO adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: When the scope of the contract changes, the Government should review and adjust the MEO to determine whether savings are still being realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Seattle security contract scope changed and MEO may not have been updated; require scope-change reviews and adjust MEO or recompete as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of readiness/exercise-related workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications/estimates should include large readiness exercise meal volumes and other predictable surges to avoid post-award modifications for added work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Food service contracts saw cost increases when readiness exercise meals were not estimated in the original contract—anticipate surge requirements in PWS and estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely planning and execution of follow-on contract awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance planning must ensure follow-on contract awards occur upon contract expiration to avoid extensions that can cause excessive cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five of six contracts experienced delays in follow-on awards leading to cost increases; improve planning and procurement timelines to avoid extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity of Contract Specialists to A-76 impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: MLCPAC Contract Specialists should be fully sensitized to the impact of A-76 contracts on the Coast Guard and be wary of excess cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviewed Contract Specialists treated A-76 contracts like regular service contracts; they should differentiate A-76 in administration and monitor ongoing cost savings compared to MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of congressional continuing resolutions on contract administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing Resolutions cause extra contract modifications and administrative burden that should be anticipated and managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three continuing resolutions in a short period required multiple modifications for partial obligations, creating an inefficient use of Contract Specialist time—track and plan for funding uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Manager qualifications and prior military experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly motivated prior military service project managers make food service contracts work well for the contractor and the customer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project managers with prior military service demonstrated quality management and cooperation; consider PM background when evaluating contractor management capabilities.
